title: Zonal Failover Conductor: adaptive triage, soft-pin admission & staged shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Production incidents in cross-region traffic show repeated oscillation between optimistic geo-hedging and capacity overcommit. Current steering is brittle to bursty tails: p99 spikes in region A cause wholesale failovers that create overload in region B. We need a conductor that coordinates soft failover, per-zonal admission gating, and prioritized shedding while preserving locality and SLOs.

Proposal: Implement a Zonal Failover Conductor (ZFC) — a logically centralized decision layer that: 1) enforces per-zone latency and error SLOs, 2) runs a tokenized admission controller with capacity-aware soft-pin rules, 3) applies circuit-breaker gates per-model-version and per-deployment tier, and 4) executes staged failover and prioritized load-shedding (graceful degradation lanes). ZFC operates as part of the global routing plane and emits deterministic routing directives that workers and edge proxies consume.

Core behaviors and thresholds (initial):
- SLOs: per-zone p95 latency target (SLO) = 120ms for interactive tiers; error budget burn tracked hourly and daily.
- Circuit breaker (zone-level): open when 5m error rate > 2% AND p95 latency > 2x SLO for 3 consecutive 1m windows.
- Soft-pin admission: prefer local zone if free_tokens_local >= 0.2 * steady_tokens, otherwise allow remote dispatch up to capacity_ratio_limit. Tokens are a soft admission currency refreshed per-second from capacity estimator.
- Hysteresis: once redirected away from a zone, require 2-minute recovery window and linear ramp back to 100% local routing over 10 minutes to avoid oscillation.
- Prioritized shedding lanes: ordered by tenant tier -> inference type (safety/diagnostic -> realtime -> background embeddings). Shedding uses fractional drop percentages computed by deficit / capacity_curve.

Telemetry and metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency per zone, error_rate, capacity_utilization, allocated_tokens, token_drain_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, queue_depth, failover_event_count, shed_rate_by_tenant. Export traces for decision path for postmortem.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- ZFC prototype in staging can route synthetic traffic and maintain p95 SLO in origin zone for 90% of steady bursts while keeping cross-zone overload below 5% extra latency.
- Circuit breaker triggers observed in staging match offline simulation for the same injected failure signals.
- Canary: Gradual rollout to 5% of traffic with observability dashboards and kill-switch.
- Runbook and post-failover checklist published and reviewed by SRE/Platform.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Design & simulation (2 sprints): build decision simulator that consumes historical traces and can run failure scenarios (zone outage, p95 spike, KV cache thrash).
2) Prototype (1 sprint): implement ZFC control API and a passive routing agent in a single region. Add metrics TTL and tracing.
3) Staging canary (1 sprint): enable on limited traffic, exercise shedding and CB open/close flows.
4) Production rollout (2 sprints): gated rollout by tenant tier, with automated rollback hooks and staged region-by-region enable.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect capacity estimation leads to unnecessary shedding. Mitigation: conservative initial token refresh (slow ramp), fallback to local admission with lower thresholds, and manual override.
- Risk: new decision plane becomes single-point-of-failure. Mitigation: ZFC is logically centralized but physically distributed with quorum-safe read-only fallback; routing agents fall back to previous steering rules if ZFC unreachable.

Operational playbook (summary):
- SRE dashboard: show zone SLO burn, open circuit breakers, active shedding lanes, and token headroom.
- On CB open: auto-mitigate by throttling non-critical lanes, notify on-call, and run automated capacity probe to verify remote headroom.
- Post-incident: capture decision traces, compare simulation outputs to actual, and tune hysteresis and thresholds.

CB behavior reproducible in staging tests for injected 5% error spikes
